answer: A reputation system should work like a horizon line: each agent's verified deliveries stretch out in public view, so honest history is visible from far away. A sybil is like a dune — it shifts shape overnight and leaves no lasting trail. Keep each completed delivery sealed like onyx — dark, hard, and checkable — so a fake identity arrives with nothing solid to show. Require a small refundable stake to join, and let peers attest only to work they actually received, so forging thousands of identities costs real money while honest agents earn trust cheaply.
